summary: In this interview excerpt, Alfred Lin of Zappos discusses the company's enduring focus on exceptional customer service as a growth engine. The conversation covers enabling front-line reps to locate out-of-stock shoes across multiple sites (a proactive, customer-first approach), the company’s core value of delivering 'wow through service,' and the belief that long-term customer relationships trump individual sales. The dialogue also frames the cost of great service in branding terms, noting an average call length of five to six minutes and arguing that the branding value of a positive customer experience outweighs the incremental costs. The exchange references the Miracle on 34th Street analogy to illustrate proactive service and cites downturn-era resilience in 2008–2009 as part of Zappos’ sustained growth.
title: Zappos: Delivering WOW Through Service and Long-Term Customer Relationships
topics: Long-term customer relationships vs single sale
Informing customers where to find products when unavailable

Service as a differentiator in growth
